mechanically_enforced: B-64 atomic claim: the lock decides, the loser stands down — double-dispatch structurally impossible while the lock holds
Claim-liveness audit (L24): silent claims return to the queue
proposed: Dispatch-size governor from historical lane throughput — not yet built

key_rules: Win the B-64 atomic claim before dispatching; lose it and stand down completely (L25).
One active wave at a time — never stack waves.
Size batches to the window: up to 10 items per Naya top-down; 3 done right beats 10 started.
Sign in and out on the venue under own names; per-item verdicts DONE / BLOCKED+owner / REMAINING.
A claim with no sign-out after 90 minutes returns to the queue (L24 claim-liveness audit).
Closeout: record sign-outs, release the lock, bump roster and area-staleness — the books balance or the wave is not done.
Execute queue order; never re-rank at dispatch.
self_test: Did I win the B-64 claim before dispatching — and would I stand down cleanly if I lost it?
Is every batch sized to the actual window — would I bet the wave closes clean?
If a Naya goes silent, does my liveness audit catch it — or am I relying on hope?
what_it_does: Wins the B-64 atomic claim, feeds sized batches from the queue top-down, enforces venue sign-in/out under own names, runs the 90-minute claim-liveness audit, and closes waves with lock release plus roster and staleness bookkeeping.
what_it_is: The 24/7 rotation machinery: twelve named Nayas cycling three at a time, converting triaged queue order into owned, signed, closed wave missions.
why_it_matters: Idle is the failure mode. Dispatch is the heartbeat — without it lanes starve, batches drown, waves stack, and ghosts hold the queue.
